source_name: CBCG — Elektronski servisi (e-service portals)
why_relevant: Index of six CBCG digital service platforms (auctions, resident reporting, enforcement/prinudna naplata systems, transaction-account registry lookups). Each portal is a separate host/application whose terms of use and technical access model must be assessed independently before any collection.

source_name: CBCG — Banke u Crnoj Gori (official bank website directory)
why_relevant: Authoritative, maintained list of every licensed bank plus its official website (and banks in liquidation). The canonical seed list for enumerating regulated publishers in this cell and for detecting entries/exits.

source_name: European Commission — TAIEX instrument and events database
why_relevant: TAIEX workshop/expert-mission records are a granular, near-real-time signal of which specific EU acts a beneficiary administration is currently working to transpose. Event listings for Montenegro on financial services would be a high-frequency leading indicator.

source_name: UBCG — member bank list ("O nama")
why_relevant: Authoritative, cheap enumeration of the full population of licensed banks in Montenegro (11 members observed: Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, NLB, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat) — the seed list for per-bank source scouting. Also enumerates the 16 committees, which is a map of which regulatory topics the sector organises around.

source_name: UBCG — Propisi (curated banking legislation page)
why_relevant: A sector-curated shortlist of the laws the banks themselves consider core (Zakon o CBCG, Zakon o bankama, Zakon o stečaju i likvidaciji banaka, ZSPNFT, Zakon o platnom prometu, Zakon o zaštiti depozita, Zakon o zaštiti potrošača) plus outbound links to CBCG, Government, securities regulator, court registry and the AML authority — a compact pointer set for the A3 regulatory perimeter.

entity_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports
source_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports — Montenegro corpus
why_relevant: Full-text searchable archive of World Bank analytical work on Montenegro (including Montenegrin-language editions, e.g. the 'Crna Gora: Priprema za prosperitet' report), development policy operations with financial-sector prior actions, and FSAP-linked technical assistance. Best single pointer for discovering less-visible assessments.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore – Odbor udruženja bankarstva, drugih finansijskih organizacija i osiguranja
why_relevant: The Chamber's banking board convenes bank representatives on regulatory topics and publishes its membership (president Miloš Miketić, Lovćen banka; secretary Almer Bećiragić). Board session agendas and Chamber announcements are an early, semi-formal channel for consultations and forthcoming obligations, and the membership list is a ready-made actor map.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council – member list (MFIC)
why_relevant: Business-association membership roster that includes both banks and their technology suppliers (Payten confirmed as a member). Membership pages carry company profiles stating Montenegro market position and client counts — a compact way to enumerate the foreign supplier ecosystem serving private banks.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — Montenegro country stream and firm article indexes
why_relevant: Trade publication for CEE legal markets: carries Montenegrin deal and regulatory items, plus per-firm article indexes that reveal which firms have an active Montenegro output. Excellent actor-mapping/snowball source for this cell.

source_name: Chambers and Partners — Global Practice Guides (Banking Regulation / Fintech)
why_relevant: Annual practitioner-written guides; where a Montenegro chapter exists it gives a structured law-and-practice narrative, and the contributor list identifies which local firms hold the banking-regulatory mandate. Montenegro chapter presence varies by year — treat as pointer until confirmed.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — financial/company profiles
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of ME company data; the ALTA PAY GROUP profile gave registered address, incorporation date (2019-10-28), director, owner and NACE activity. Useful to enrich the operator map without repeated registry queries.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — registry profile of Udruženje banaka Crne Gore
why_relevant: Commercial registry aggregator giving the association's legal identity, registered address (Novaka Miloševa BB, Podgorica) and registration date (2003), plus officer data. Useful for entity resolution and for confirming legal form when the association's own site is thin — and the same aggregator can resolve every member bank and adviser found via the association directories.

source_name: euprava.me service catalogue – institutional identity/contact records
why_relevant: The e-government service catalogue holds per-institution records (address, competences, services) including for the AML directorate and the Anti-Corruption Agency. Useful for resolving official names, successor bodies and current contact points when institutions are reorganised — a recurring problem in Montenegro.

source_name: IFLR1000 — Montenegro jurisdiction and firm rankings
why_relevant: Directory that enumerates the Montenegrin firms ranked for banking & finance (Prelevic, JPM & Partners, Vujacic and others). Not commentary itself, but the authoritative shortlist of which advisory sites to monitor for client alerts.

source_name: ILO NATLEX / N-Lex — international mirrors of Montenegrin legislation
why_relevant: International legal-information gateways that index national gazette texts and describe how to query the national collection. Value is as a fallback pointer and English-language entry point when the national gazette site is bot-defended; coverage of financial-sector law is partial and often lagged.

source_name: Advokatska komora Crne Gore (Bar Association of Montenegro) — member directory
why_relevant: Official roster of admitted advocates and offices in Podgorica and other towns. Not commentary, but the exhaustive local-language actor list from which to identify small Montenegrin firms with banking practices that no international directory ranks.

entity_name: Google Play / Apple App Store listings for Montenegrin bank apps
source_name: Google Play / Apple App Store listings for Montenegrin bank apps (vendor fingerprint via bundle IDs)
why_relevant: App package identifiers leak the underlying platform vendor: NLB ProKlik Crna Gora ships under 'hr.asseco.android.jimba…', i.e. Asseco's Jimba/mToken mobile framework. Systematically enumerating bundle IDs, developer accounts and SDK signatures for all Montenegrin bank apps yields a vendor map that no press release provides.

source_name: Halcom – list of banks using Halcom (e-banking / qualified digital certificates)
why_relevant: Halcom publishes the roster of banks running its Hal E-Bank corporate e-banking and certificate infrastructure — an explicit vendor customer list covering the Adriatic region, useful for establishing Montenegrin installed base and for tracking displacement (Erste Bank Montenegro is publicly migrating off Halcom to eMon OfficeBanking).

source_name: ICT Cortex – Montenegrin ICT cluster member directory
why_relevant: Cluster of Montenegrin software firms (Amplitudo, Bild Studio, Čikom, Logate, Codepixel, Fleka, Oykos, Data Design and others) categorised by capability including BI/data. Several of these firms build and maintain systems for Montenegrin banks, so the directory is the entry point to the domestic supplier layer that never appears in international vendor press.

source_name: Komora javnih izvršitelja Crne Gore — imenik izvršitelja i propisi
why_relevant: Official directory of public bailiffs (the enforcement channel banks use for retail/SME debt) plus a curated 'propisi' and 'načelni pravni stavovi' section that archives enforcement-law texts and binding legal positions.

source_name: Legal 500 — Montenegro leading firms (banking & finance)
why_relevant: Second, independent directory for actor mapping in a small market where the set of firms writing banking-regulatory commentary is only a dozen or so; also hosts country comparative guides written by local firms.

source_name: Lexology — Montenegro banking/payments contributor library
why_relevant: Aggregates client alerts from many firms covering Montenegro (Karanovic, and others) in one searchable, dated stream — the single most efficient way to discover which firms are commenting on a given Montenegrin rule, and to snowball to new actors. Registration-walled for some content.

source_name: Mastercard partner / vendor directories (Engage, acceptance and processing partners)
why_relevant: Scheme-side partner enumeration equivalent to Visa's; a first-principles source because certification is a precondition for serving banks, so the directory reveals the eligible supplier pool even when no deal is announced. Not yet verified for Montenegro-specific filtering.

source_name: NVOinfo — NGO registry entry for Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore
why_relevant: Montenegrin NGO directory; because most Montenegrin associations, institutes and professional bodies are registered as NGOs, this directory is a systematic pointer for discovering additional finance-adjacent associations and consumer bodies that do not surface in ordinary search.

source_name: Paragraf Lex (RS and BA legal databases)
why_relevant: Commercial consolidated-legislation aggregators for Serbia (paragraf.rs) and BiH (paragraf.ba) that expose current, amended texts of banking and central-bank laws with amendment history — far easier to diff than official gazettes, and the fastest way to see what regional wording Montenegrin drafters are borrowing.

source_name: Visa Partner Directory (Visa Ready certified partners, incl. issuer processors)
why_relevant: Filterable directory of certified issuer processors, POS/acceptance and fintech partners by capability and region — a systematic way to enumerate which vendors are certified to serve Montenegrin issuers/acquirers, rather than guessing from press releases.
